reason: Conversation 2 quickly asked the right question after learning the kettle and fridge worked, suggesting a switched spur or isolator near the cupboard. That led the homeowner to find the 'washer' switch off and turn it back on, so the machine was fixed in a few turns. Conversation 1 gave US-style advice (GFCI, breaker), repeatedly suggested checking the plug, taps and back panel that the user had said she could not reach, and gave irrelevant suggestions (child lock, dials, tapping the cord). It also floated control board failure, which is unsupported, and never mentioned the switched spur, and several of its replies were truncated. Conversation 2 did have a minor flaw: it asked for the model number and showed a replacement-part prompt that was not needed. Even so, it finished cleanly with a sensible tip to label the switch.
